This academic performance in the later stage of your studies signaled to the model a high likelihood of struggling with the bar exam.

Next, your choice to attend law school part-time also contributed toward predicting failure, though with less force. The vast majority (93%) of accepted students planned to study full-time, so your part-time status worked against you.

Finally, your first-year class ranking added further weight toward rejection. Ranking in the third decile is noticeably below the average sixth-decile performance of accepted students.

Taken together, these academic and enrollment patterns led the model to conclude you are unlikely to pass the bar on the first try. To improve your chances, focus on strengthening your academic record if possible, consider switching to full-time study, and look into bar-preparation resources or alternative admissions pathways that place less emphasis on first-time bar passage. Reapplying after addressing these areas could meaningfully change your outcome.
